character.lede: A lake house climbs in four stepped tiers, from a teal-brick garage podium to dark timber penthouse boxes. An octagonal plunge pool crowns the podium, and the rooms below hold a gym and a wine cellar.

spots.line: An exercise bike, a bench and a yoga mat fill the gym.
Wine racks and two bar stools line the cellar.
A workbench and a bicycle share the podium garage.

facts.style: Four stepped tiers on a lake lot: a teal-brick garage podium, a raised main floor reached up an exterior stair between stepped timber planters, three dark timber bays, an octagonal plunge pool on the podium roof, corner balconies with timber rails and two offset dark-timber penthouse boxes with copper ends, all under thin dark flat roofs

character.truths: The Core sits on a credenza in the Living room. There is no television in this house: never say TV. Kitchen has an island. The plunge pool is on the podium roof; balconies have timber rails.

details.rule: every beat of an adult or teen persona (13 or older) gets a detail (before, after, steps, fact); pair beats first

gitea: [note] Gitea Mirror is a different listing (it copies GitHub repositories into Gitea). Name only Gitea. Forgejo does the same job; name one Git host per household.
[note] The listing mentions Actions CI. The package ships the forge and its database only, no runner, so do not show a CI run.
[claims] Say where the repositories are (on the Core). Do not say it syncs with, or is compatible with, GitHub.
Listing mentions Actions CI; no runner ships: never show a CI run.
Gitea Mirror is a different app.
immich: [note] Bundles its own database and a machine-learning service, so first start takes a while.
[note] No API is mentioned in the listing; treat as web interface only for agent purposes.
akaunting: [claims] Bookkeeping tool. No accounting, tax or legal advice.
marketplace: Source-available (Business Source License). Seafile and others carry umbrel strings: the admin email default is a placeholder address on umbrel.local.
navidrome: Description says "from anywhere" and "works offline-first": paraphrase, remote access is not claimed
Already in 11 of 30 stories: one short of the cap of 12; rotate music beats to mStream, Swing Music and Music Assistant
homehub: No passwords: a "Select your user" box offers every name including Administrator (anyone on the network can pick one)
Extras bundled: recipes, expiry tracker, link shortener, PDF compressor, QR generator
obsidian: [licence] Obsidian is not open source. Do not call it open source.
[note] An Obsidian MCP entry exists so an agent can read and write the vault.
not open source (catalog: never say so)
listing says private and offline: do not repeat
notes are files on the Core, the app is streamed
anything-llm: [cloud-link] Works with local or cloud models. Pick the local one in the story.
Works with local or cloud models: pick Ollama (the default) in the story.
Telemetry is disabled by default in the Hub package (good).
Per app multi user with permissions: fine as one household login set.
open-notebook: [cloud-link] Supports 18 plus providers including cloud ones. Ollama is the local path.
[heavy] Podcast-style audio overviews need a speech model.
Install form has OpenAI, Anthropic, Google and Groq key fields: leave blank; Ollama is the local path.
Podcast style audio overviews need a speech model: do not mention.
Capture shows sample notebook content, not personal data.
linkwarden: Sharing links publicly needs inbound reach: keep the story to saving, not sharing
The Pocket name in replaces is stale
steam-headless: [cloud-link] Steam needs a Valve account to sign in, and the game library and the purchases are Valve's. The Core runs the session; the account stays with Valve. Say that, never "no account".

[hardware] The listing asks for GPU passthrough for best performance and the Hub package declares no GPU device, so a given Core may not run a given game well. Say what the Core does (it runs the session at home), never

[claims] No frame rate, resolution or latency figure, and not "smooth". Never "gaming PC", "console replacement" or "cloud gaming replacement" in the text. The chip may read "replaces GeForce Now" or "replaces Xbox Cloud

[note] It shows a streamed desktop with sound in a browser (noVNC), so the screen needs a browser, not a console. The container runs privileged with host access: do not call it sandboxed. Keep the stream on the home netw
[note] Persona decision 2026-10-15 (Liam Broza): re-admitted from the old cloud-account exclusion for the gamer archetype, with the caveats above.
wingfit: QA shot is a sign-in wall with an error toast
beatsync: Rights to the music are the household's; the app plays what you upload
Do not print the millisecond-accurate sync claim or any timing figure
Public URL field is optional; leave it blank for home-network use
frigate: [hardware] Needs IP cameras that stream over RTSP. Cameras are not part of the Core.
[public-access] Watching cameras from away from home is remote access, which the sheet leaves unfinished.
[claims] No detection-speed or accuracy numbers. Do not say it prevents anything.
QA screenshot shows "No frames have been received, check error logs": reject. The store listing image shows a real backyard photo that is not a Hub capture.
Watching away from home is remote access: not claimed.
docuseal: [claims] Do not call signatures legally binding.
[note] Signers outside your home network need access to your Core.
Do not call signatures legally binding
cyberchef: Listing says nothing pasted is ever sent anywhere and that it works with no internet connection: do not repeat either (sec-never-leaves, sec-offline)
A tool, not a store of anything: nothing is held after the tab closes
syncthing: [qa] No QA screenshot on origin/main (e2e/screenshots). It is listed and installable, but nobody has recorded a verified run.
mindustry: [note] Headless game server; no web interface. Players use the game client.
[claims] No frame rate or player-count claims.
[qa] No QA screenshot on origin/main (e2e/screenshots). It is listed and installable, but nobody has recorded a verified run.
Headless: the household needs a console to run commands such as host and gameover
blockbench: Projects live in the browser (IndexedDB) or in files the person saves: the Core serves the app, it does not hold the models
The listing names Minecraft models; say "game models" or "block models" in copy
Free-text store claim "never sees your models" is accurate for the container
habitica: The sign-up page in the capture carries a cookie-consent banner: check the self-hosted build for analytics scripts before saying it sends nothing out
Game, not a health or behaviour tool: no outcomes
tldraw: not open source (tldraw licence; a production watermark shows)
solidtime: [qa] No QA screenshot on origin/main (e2e/screenshots). It is listed and installable, but nobody has recorded a verified run.
listing mentions invoices: say nothing about billing or tax
teampass: [qa] No QA screenshot on origin/main (e2e/screenshots). It is listed and installable, but nobody has recorded a verified run.
Listing claims secrets never leave the appliance (banned word, banned claim)
Per-person roles sit close to the cap-multi-user rule: phrase it as the app's folders and permissions
invoice-ninja: [cloud-link] Taking card payments needs a payment provider. Say invoicing, not payment processing.
